reason: The official CameraAccess sample derives hasActiveDevice from AutoDeviceSelector.activeDeviceStream. Compare this public selection path with an exact owned mock-ID filter after the Specific selector/session diagnostic showed connected, registered and exact IDs but still failed at session start.
verifiedContract: DeviceIdentifier is String; DeviceFilter is @Sendable (Device) -> Bool.
AutoDeviceSelector.init(wearables: any WearablesInterface, filter: DeviceFilter? = nil) is in the pinned public interface.
The filter captures only the immutable owned mock identifier and accepts only exact identifier equality.
The selector is retained on the model. Existing exact-ID, epoch, cancellation, permission and timeout guards remain.
Extra diagnostics before selector wait and at the existing watchdog make a no-selection result observable without changing the timer.
The acceptance test is byte-identical to the already reviewed diagnostic version.
rejectedInference: The public interface does not reveal whether SpecificDeviceSelector.activeDevice merely returns the configured ID.
The sample does not establish .compatible as an explicit start requirement; no compatibility wait or state override is introduced.
The public AnyAsyncSequence interface alone does not prove exact cancellation timing; epoch fencing and SDK disable remain in place.
result: No P1/P2 findings in the complete 39-line selector-control patch. One source-bound execution of the unchanged acceptance case is admitted; this record is not a runtime pass.
limits: A source-guided control experiment, not a proven SDK root cause or repair before execution.
No physical-device, production-host, SAM/NVIDIA, release or deployment qualification.
